The emitted C spells exactly that condition, but the project's flag set may let wcc386 hoist the invariant product out of the loop, which would make the rebuilt loop a couple of instructions shorter per tile than the original. It is a contract-D style difference and I could not settle whether the flag set actually hoists it.
00010b20.needs: Disassemble the loop in the built MOVEGRID.OBJ and compare its shape against 00010b5e-00010b85. If the product is hoisted and that is judged to matter, the fix is a flag-set question rather than a source one -- the source already spells the recomputation.
00010b20.answer: SETTLED, no hoist. The built object recomputes the product in the loop head exactly as 00010b20 does. Disassembled the code bytes of the existing workspace/code_emit/out/objs/MOVEGRID.OBJ (LEDATA payload at file offset 0x0192; the object holds only fdps_map_grid_reset): the loop head at payload +0x3e (file offset 0x1d0) is 8b 45 f8 / 0f af 45 f4 / 3b 45 f0 / 7f 07 / eb 18 = MOV EAX,[EBP-0x8] / IMUL EAX,[EBP-0xc] / CMP EAX,[EBP-0x10] / JG body / JMP epilogue -- five instructions, the same SHAPE as 00010b5e-00010b6a with the IMUL inside the head and re-executed every pass. Not the same operands: the original reads the product out of [EBP-0x10] and compares against [EBP-0x8], the rebuild the other way round, because the two frame slots are assigned in the other order (see residual). That is which slot holds what, not whether the multiply is in the loop, which is the only thing this concern asked. The reason is the flag set itself: rebuild_info/build_flags.md fixes it at 'wcc386 -bt=dos4g -mf -4s -fpi -s -ot -od', and -od turns the optimiser off (the same flag that keeps every local written back to the stack, which this object also shows -- both dimension slots and the index are re-read from the frame in the head). No loop-invariant motion runs, so there is nothing to hoist the product out. The emitted C needed no change and gets none: it already spells the recomputation, and the built code proves the spelling survives the toolchain. Contract D closes for this loop.
00010b20.settled_by: workspace/code_emit/out/objs/MOVEGRID.OBJ (already built by the emit round; disassembled read-only, nothing rebuilt) plus rebuild_info/build_flags.md's -ot -od determination. Rescan of 00010b20.
00010b20.residual: Residual, non-blocking, found by the same byte-for-byte comparison and recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it. Two shape differences remain between the built object and 00010b20, neither functional (ADR-0001 is functional equivalence, not byte-exact), and both outside what this concern asked: (1) frame slot assignment differs -- the original puts width at [EBP-0x10] and the index at [EBP-0x8], the rebuild puts width at [EBP-0x8] and the index at [EBP-0x10], which is declaration order and nothing else; (2) the original's increment block at 00010b6c is MOV EAX,[EBP-0x8] / INC [EBP-0x8], while the rebuild emits the INC alone -- one dead load per tile. EAX is dead across it in the original (reloaded at 00010b74 before any use), so no value and no flag crosses the difference. Both are codegen shape, not behaviour; neither is a defect in the emitted C and neither is a reason to touch it.
